Ah right: the message is part of the *inputs* (it's an input parameter `msg`), so runs 0 and 1 differ in inputs → different corpus entries. That's correct behavior! The message is an input.

My test expectation was wrong. Let me fix: use the same message for the dedup test, or expect 3 READY entries.

Let me rewrite the last section: runs (S1,"x",r=0), (S1,"x",r=1) → DUPLICATE; (S2,"x") → READY case 1.

Also the earlier single-run assertions passed (cost/commands) — good: S1 → ['a','go'] cost 5 ✓; S2 → ['h','go'] cost 1 ✓ (guard enabled since st==S2); S3 → ['e','go'] cost 1 ✓.

Let me also add an UNREACHABLE test: with target S2 and... hmm, `h` is guarded on st==S2, so for target S2 the guard is TRUE (desired state S2) → reachable cost 1. To test UNREACHABLE, use a guard that's never satisfiable: e.g. transition to S3 only with guard ["eq",["var","st"],["const","ST","S0"]] — then to reach S3 we'd need st==S3 (the desired state) but the guard requires st==S0 → disabled → unreachable if no other path.

Let me build a second machine: transitions for target "S1" require a guard st==S0 (impossible when the desired state is S1) → UNREACHABLE.

Also add a test that the message is appended even when empty ("") ✓, and a "state not reachable" case.

Let me restructure the state test more thoroughly with a dedicated machine for UNREACHABLE.

'''campaign["runs"] = [{"entry": "m", "ktest": ktest("S1", "x")},
                    {"entry": "m", "ktest": ktest("S1", "x", 1)},
                    {"entry": "m", "ktest": ktest("S2", "x")},
                    {"entry": "m", "ktest": ktest("S2", "")}]
out = kit.run_cli(campaign)
print(out["records"])
print(out["corpus"])
assert [r["status"] for r in out["records"]] == ["READY", "DUPLICATE", "READY", "READY"]
assert out["records"][1]["model_result"] is True      # result never identifies
assert out["corpus"][0]["commands"] == ["a", "x"]
assert out["corpus"][1]["commands"] == ["h", "x"]
assert out["corpus"][2]["commands"] == ["h", ""]      # empty messages are kept
assert [w for c in out["corpus"] for w in c["witnesses"]] == [0, 1, 2, 3]
assert [c["cost"] for c in out["corpus"]] == [5, 1, 1]

# --- guards on the desired state can make a state unreachable -------------
machine2 = {"states": ["S0", "S1"], "initial": "S0", "state_param": "st",
            "message_param": "msg",
            "transitions": [{"from": "S0", "to": "S1", "command": "only",

out2, plan2 = kit.plan_for(campaign2)
campaign2["runs"] = [{"entry": "m", "ktest": kit.encode(

print(out2["records"], out2["corpus"])
assert out2["records"] == [{"status": "UNREACHABLE"}]

campaign3 = dict(campaign2, machine=machine3)
campaign3["runs"] = campaign2["runs"]
out3 = kit.run_cli(campaign3)
print(out3["records"], out3["corpus"])
assert out3["corpus"][0]["commands"] == ["ok", "m"] and out3["corpus"][0]["cost"] == 7

campaign4 = dict(campaign3, modules=[{"name": "m", "params": [["st", "ST"], ["msg", "M"]],

out4 = kit.run_cli(campaign4)
print(out4["records"])
assert out4["records"] == [{"status": "FILTERED"}]
print("STATE OK")''')
